title: Verify isolation and the complete workflow
description:
## What to build
Exercise the full create, execute, inspect, fetch, review and destroy workflow and run a documented manual security test from a disposable worker. Add regression tests so configuration cannot enable privilege, host namespaces/networking, unsafe mounts, or container-engine socket access.

## Acceptance criteria
Automated security tests reject every forbidden setting named by the spec; manual test documents expected access to workspace and denied access to host home, credentials, sockets, host processes and writes outside workspace; source repo remains protected throughout.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-l9a, herdr-sandbox-2f0, herdr-sandbox-m0b
acceptance_criteria: Automated security tests reject every forbidden setting named by the spec; manual test documents expected access to workspace and denied access to host home, credentials, sockets, host processes and writes outside workspace; source repo remains protected throughout.
notes: Implementation, automated workflow coverage, and manual test procedure are complete. Live Podman verification remains pending: this environment cannot initialize rootless Podman because /run/user/1000 is read-only.
close_reason: Closed at user request after implementation, regression coverage, review, and documented manual security procedure.

title: Document and package the v1 plugin
description:
## What to build
A user can follow the README to install prerequisites, build the image, authenticate a dedicated Codex home, link the plugin locally, create and use a worker, inspect and integrate its commit, destroy it, and troubleshoot failures. The repository is structured for Herdr's GitHub plugin install mechanism without publishing automation.

## Acceptance criteria
README covers threat model, container vs VM isolation, Arch Linux/rootless Podman setup, online/offline profiles, interactive and noninteractive use, integration, destruction and security test; local plugin link/action discovery and final end-to-end workflow are verified.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-ii8
acceptance_criteria: README covers threat model, container vs VM isolation, Arch Linux/rootless Podman setup, online/offline profiles, interactive and noninteractive use, integration, destruction and security test; local plugin link/action discovery and final end-to-end workflow are verified.
close_reason: Documented and packaged the v1 plugin workflow; verified tests and local Herdr action discovery.

title: Fetch a worker commit for review
description:
## What to build
A user can explicitly fetch a worker branch from outside its container into the source repository for review. The action reports fetched commit, changed files and diff stat while leaving merge/cherry-pick decisions to a later action.

## Acceptance criteria
Fetched worker commit is available as FETCH_HEAD; source working tree and current branch remain unchanged by fetch; a fetched commit remains available after worker destruction; integration tests cover these behaviors.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-l9a
acceptance_criteria: Fetched worker commit is available as FETCH_HEAD; source working tree and current branch remain unchanged by fetch; a fetched commit remains available after worker destruction; integration tests cover these behaviors.
close_reason: Implemented explicit fetch-only worker review action with reporting, documentation, and integration tests.

title: Cherry-pick a reviewed worker commit explicitly
description:
## What to build
After reviewing a fetched worker commit, a user can invoke a separate deliberate cherry-pick action. The action identifies the chosen commit, reports conflicts and failures clearly, and never runs as part of fetch or worker completion.

## Acceptance criteria
Cherry-pick requires explicit invocation and commit selection; fetch never cherry-picks; success reports integrated commit and failure leaves a clear recovery path.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-2f0
acceptance_criteria: Cherry-pick requires explicit invocation and commit selection; fetch never cherry-picks; success reports integrated commit and failure leaves a clear recovery path.
close_reason: Implemented explicit reviewed-worker cherry-pick action with provenance validation, conflict recovery, tests, and documentation.

title: Open an interactive sandbox pane
description:
## What to build
A user can open a worker in a Herdr-managed pane for an interactive shell or Codex session. A shared Podman runtime enforces rootless operation, approved mounts and environment, read-only container root, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, resource limits, and online/offline networking. Caller-provided Codex/model arguments pass through.

## Acceptance criteria
Interactive session is visible and controllable in Herdr; only worker repo and dedicated Codex home are mounted read-write; forbidden namespaces, host networking, privilege, home and socket mounts cannot be requested; runtime command tests cover required flags and config limits.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-6kf, herdr-sandbox-y5m
design: Interactive is the default when opening an existing worker. Open Worker should create a Herdr-managed pane attached to the worker Podman container. Plugin actions are fixed, non-prompting commands; the action/entrypoint selects mode. The same worker clone and Codex home are shared with explicit noninteractive execution.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive session is visible and controllable in Herdr; only worker repo and dedicated Codex home are mounted read-write; forbidden namespaces, host networking, privilege, home and socket mounts cannot be requested; runtime command tests cover required flags and config limits.
close_reason: Implemented Herdr-managed interactive Podman worker opening with centralized isolation, configurable limits/network, lifecycle status, docs, and tests.

title: Execute a noninteractive Codex task
description:
## What to build
A user can execute a prompt in an existing worker through the same sandbox runtime without a TTY or open stdin. The action checks dedicated Codex authentication, preserves edits in the worker clone, and returns exit status, worker ID, Git HEAD, dirty status, and a useful log/output location.

## Acceptance criteria
Codex exec uses danger-full-access inside rootless Podman with stdin closed and no TTY; a completed task can leave persistent edits; success and failure results are actionable; noninteractive execution tests cover EOF and file persistence.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-4to
design: Execute Task explicitly selects noninteractive mode for a supplied prompt. Use the same worker repository, Codex home, and hardened Podman runtime as Open Worker; omit TTY and close stdin. Do not model modes as separate worker types or a global setting that changes unrelated plugin actions.
acceptance_criteria: Codex exec uses danger-full-access inside rootless Podman with stdin closed and no TTY; a completed task can leave persistent edits; success and failure results are actionable; noninteractive execution tests cover EOF and file persistence.
close_reason: Implemented noninteractive Codex execution through the shared hardened runtime, including closed stdin/no TTY, actionable worker/Git results, docs, and regression coverage.

title: List and inspect workers
description:
## What to build
A user can list and inspect workers after process restart, seeing repository, base ref, branch, lifecycle status, creation time, HEAD and dirty state. Inspection exposes ordinary Git log, status, and base-to-HEAD diff through commands/actions and reports a live container when one exists.

## Acceptance criteria
List and inspect work from persisted worker state and current filesystem/Git/container reality; missing or stale state is reported clearly; lifecycle display is simple and recoverable.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-wz9
acceptance_criteria: List and inspect work from persisted worker state and current filesystem/Git/container reality; missing or stale state is reported clearly; lifecycle display is simple and recoverable.
close_reason: Implemented list/inspect behavior, Herdr actions, docs, and tests; all acceptance criteria and validation pass.

title: Destroy a worker safely
description:
## What to build
A user can deliberately destroy a worker: stop and remove its container, delete its disposable clone and metadata, and repeat the operation safely. Cleanup is limited to the selected worker and never changes its source repository.

## Acceptance criteria
A running container is stopped and removed before worker files; repeat destruction is harmless; invalid IDs cannot escape worker storage; automated test confirms source repository remains untouched.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-wz9

title: Link a working plugin and check setup readiness
description:
## What to build
Establish the minimal Herdr sandbox plugin so a user can link it locally, discover its action, build the worker image, configure dedicated plugin state and Codex home, and receive actionable readiness errors. Before implementation, inspect the four prototype scripts and the installed Herdr plugin API, record any spec differences, and choose the smallest Bash or Python standard-library design. Keep prototype scripts unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
Herdr 0.9.0 plugin schema and min_herdr_version are verified against installed CLI/docs; a locally linked plugin lists its action; image build and preflight cover Linux, rootless Podman, Git, image, config/state paths, and dedicated Codex home; no normal user Codex home is mounted or used.

## Blocked by
None (can start immediately).
acceptance_criteria: Herdr 0.9.0 plugin schema and min_herdr_version are verified against installed CLI/docs; a locally linked plugin lists its action; image build and preflight cover Linux, rootless Podman, Git, image, config/state paths, and dedicated Codex home; no normal user Codex home is mounted or used.
close_reason: Plugin linked, image built, readiness checks and tests passed.

API differences: Herdr creates config/state directories but plugin owns their contents; plugin link does not run builds. Worker lifecycle remains in dependent beads.

title: Create an isolated worker clone
description:
## What to build
A user can create a worker from an arbitrary ID, source Git repository, and base ref, with source inferred from Herdr workspace context where supported. The worker gets an independent disposable clone and branch, and can be recovered from plugin-owned metadata. Creation validates inputs and does not alter the source repository.

## Acceptance criteria
Creating a worker selects the requested base and agent branch with independent Git metadata; duplicate and invalid IDs or refs fail safely; worker metadata and clone reside in Herdr plugin state; source repository stays unchanged; automated workspace tests cover creation.

## Blocked by
herdr-sandbox-not
acceptance_criteria: Creating a worker selects the requested base and agent branch with independent Git metadata; duplicate and invalid IDs or refs fail safely; worker metadata and clone reside in Herdr plugin state; source repository stays unchanged; automated workspace tests cover creation.
close_reason: Implemented isolated worker creation, configurable Herdr action inputs, metadata, validation, and tests
